original_question: Suppose {f_k}_{k=0}^n is a finite Polya frequency sequence of order d >= r. Must the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomial P_n^r(z) be Hurwitz stable, meaning that all of its zeros lie in the open left half-plane?
target_in_paper: Dmitrii Karp, subsection "Toeplitz determinants of Pochhammers" in arXiv:2312.07754, Conjecture 3. This is the paper's specific Hurwitz-stability conjecture for the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomial P_n^r, as opposed to the neighboring real-negative-zero conjectures.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper: the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomial P_n^r and the conjectured conclusion that it is Hurwitz stable. It also correctly ties the hypothesis to finite Pólya frequency sequences and uses the intended stability notion "all zeros lie in the open left half-plane."
missing_details: The paper does not treat P_n^r as a free-standing polynomial symbol; it is defined through coefficient extraction from a higher-order Toeplitz determinant generating function.
One must define f(x;z) = sum_{k>=0} f_k (x)_k z^k / k!, where (x)_k is the rising factorial (Pochhammer symbol).
One must define F_r(x,z) = det[f(x+j-i;z)]_{i,j=1}^r and then write F_r(x,z) = sum_{m>=0} z^m P_m^r(x); the conjecture concerns the coefficient polynomial P_n^r(x).
The official wording uses x as the polynomial variable; z is the auxiliary generating variable. Your draft uses P_n^r(z), which blurs that distinction.
The official hypothesis is stated with the sequence in PF_r (not phrased as PF_d with d >= r), so the stand-alone question should use the paper's exact PF_r formulation.
To make PF_r stand-alone, one should say that the Toeplitz matrix [f_{j-i}] with f_k = 0 outside the index range has all minors of size at most r nonnegative.
The quantifier r >= 2 should be stated explicitly.
The paper's official sentence appends the consequence "In particular, it has positive coefficients," which is part of the intended scope even though the main question is Hurwitz stability.
refined_question:
Let r >= 2 and define f(x;z) = sum_{k>=0} f_k (x)_k z^k/k!, where (x)_k is the rising factorial. Form the Toeplitz determinant
F_r(x,z) = det[f(x+j-i;z)]_{i,j=1}^r = sum_{m>=0} z^m P_m^r(x).
Suppose the finite sequence {f_0,f_1,...,f_n} is a Pólya frequency sequence of order r, i.e. after extending by f_k = 0 outside {0,1,...,n}, all minors of order at most r of the Toeplitz matrix [f_{j-i}] are nonnegative. Must the coefficient polynomial P_n^r(x) be Hurwitz stable, meaning that every zero of P_n^r lies in the open left half-plane Re x < 0 (and hence, in particular, P_n^r has positive coefficients)?
justification: The draft is targeting the specific Hurwitz-stability problem stated as Conjecture 3 in Dmitrii Karp's subsection of arXiv:2312.07754, not the neighboring conjectures about having only real negative zeros. The 2023 paper gives the compressed official statement but suppresses the full notation in the ar5iv rendering and explicitly says that further details are in Karp's cited paper [1]. To make the question genuinely stand-alone while staying narrow and paper-faithful, the key repair is to restore the determinant-based definition of P_n^r, distinguish the polynomial variable x from the generating variable z, and state the PF_r hypothesis in the Toeplitz-minor form. I did not broaden the question to PF_infinity or to the stronger real-negative-zero conjecture, because that would move from the exact Hurwitz-stability conjecture to a different neighboring problem.
